requestedActions.title: List file names in the connected customer's App Folder
Let connected customers authorize the app to access their App Folder via OAuth

guide.summary: The confirmed request is a user-scoped OAuth integration. Each connected customer authorizes the app through the code flow, and the app receives a user token. Listing App Folder file names needs the files.metadata.read scope, which the list_folder documentation names as required. The App Folder access type limits calls to the app folder. Content download and write scopes are not requested, which fits the prohibitions. Setup in the App Console, redirect configuration and provider review remain untested. Whether other customer organizations or team administrators must approve the connection is not covered by the supplied sources.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: Each connected customer authorizes a user OAuth 2.0 token
findings.detail: Apps requesting only User API scopes receive a token associated with the user who authorizes the app. The app accesses Dropbox on behalf of each user through an OAuth flow, and the authorization code is exchanged at /oauth2/token. Customers connect through the OAuth flow and do not register their own Dropbox app.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer organization connects its own Dropbox account to the app.

evidence.quote: Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.
Do not instruct your users to register their own Dropbox application to use your app - you just need to register your app once. Your end-users will connect to that
/oauth2/token Description This endpoint applies to apps using the authorization code flow or client credentials flow. An app calls this endpoint to acquire a refresh token and/or access token.

findings.title: Register the app and configure exact redirect URIs before OAuth testing
findings.detail: The app must be registered in the App Console to obtain the app key and secret, and the exact redirect URIs must be registered there. Dropbox checks the redirect_uri at authorization time. The redirect is optional for the code flow, but the client secret must be kept secure or PKCE used instead.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first authorization test for the connect action.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you’ll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the App Console
You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the App Console
When using the code flow, your app must keep the client_secret secure. If your app can’t guarantee it’s security, then we recommend the use of PKCE as described below

findings.title: files.metadata.read covers list_folder and list_folder/continue
findings.detail: The list_folder endpoint requires files.metadata.read, and list_folder/continue requires the same scope. Both use a user Bearer token. This scope is the required grant for listing entries and does not cover downloading or writing file contents.
findings.appliesWhen: The app lists file names by calling list_folder and paginating with list_folder/continue.

OR Authorization Bearer OAuth 2.0 token issued to a specific user. Use Authorization: Bearer <token> .

findings.title: Select App Folder access so listing is rooted to the app folder
findings.detail: With App Folder access, the app can take actions allowed by its scopes only on data within its app folder. Calls are rooted to the app folder, and paths outside it are not accessible. This is the access type selected when creating the app.
findings.appliesWhen: The app should list only the connected customer's App Folder.

findings.title: Requesting more scope than needed may affect provider app review
findings.detail: Dropbox advises requesting only the least permissions required. Requesting more scope and content access than required may result in end users not accepting the OAuth request and could impact the app review process. The supplied sources do not give a review duration.
findings.appliesWhen: Before submitting the app for provider review or broader distribution.

steps.title: List App Folder entries for the test customer
steps.detail: Call list_folder with path set to the empty string (App Folder root) and recursive set to false. Representative input: path empty string and recursive false; no limit parameter is used because the supplied documentation does not define one. Expected result: HTTP 200 with entries containing file and folder names, a cursor, and has_more. If has_more is true, continue with list_folder/continue until has_more is false. File contents are not requested.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 is returned with entries containing names, a cursor, and has_more. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against files.metadata.read; confirm the outgoing request log contains only list_folder and list_folder/continue calls and no download or write requests.

steps.title: Continue listing App Folder entries until has_more is false
steps.detail: While has_more is true, call list_folder/continue with the cursor from the prior response until has_more is false. This continuation request carries the cursor returned by the prior list_folder call.
steps.doneWhen: A response returns has_more false, and all pages have been retrieved. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
